scope_notes.note: Task 6 owns the RSS session document and recovery rules over the accepted Task5 store. The Core dependency is pinned to cdb0b798d631cd7ffab6dfed3fe4b69381ed3340; the App installs its ordered object-entry codec once through the normal standard catalog/open_registry path so `tasks`/`cookies` member order and task-queue order survive a decoded VmMap. Session serialization reads the real store order and cookie runtime order; loading merges into the existing table without clearing it, keeps inner GUIDs, re-queues every document entry without de-duplication, re-parses gid/sethash from the URL, and applies the real scan rules (marker/archive/nonzero/zero removal/download range) through named `xeh_fs` primitives bounded by trusted download roots. File authority is separated: Core read roots are only the currently existing exact session/legacy files (refreshed by `session_paths`, never their parents); `write_atomic` targets only the exact session path and refuses over-budget UTF-8 payloads before staging; `stat`/`remove_zero_file`/`rename_atomic` use only explicit download roots and refuse the reserved exact session/legacy files even when a root overlaps their directory. A zero-byte image symlink removes the passed link and keeps its target. Reads and atomic saves share the single 16 MiB `SESSION_READ_LIMIT_BYTES`; the accepted Core Reader bound is the hard read limit, and an exact-size precheck keeps a known oversized file from opening a handle. Scan restore pre-checks every `filelist` task total against a trusted aggregate budget (default 100000 fids) before any stat/zero deletion/Root publication; negative, overflowing or over-budget totals are the stable `session:scan_budget` refusal.
